title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, tool schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Ava Martinez
commits: 5 commits: initial adapter and schema mapper; add tool_choice handling and deterministic selection logic; streaming message formatting for partial tool outputs; SDK samples and docs; tests and flaky-test fix
description:
Context and motivation: Add full OpenAI functions/tool-calling compatibility for (1) tool_choice semantics, (2) mapping OpenAI-style JSON schemas to Redwood tool parameter definitions, and (3) predictable message formatting for tool invocation and tool output streaming. This PR implements the compatibility layer in redwood-openai-compat, hooks the runtime tool executor to emit OpenAI-compatible messages when a tool is selected, and updates SDK examples and docs.

What this PR does: Implements a deterministic tool_choice resolution flow that mirrors OpenAI behavior (string-based choice + optional tool metadata). Adds a schema-mapper that converts OpenAI function schemas (JSON Schema-like) into Redwood tool param descriptors (type, required, defaults, enum mapping). Ensures that unknown/extra fields are surfaced via a structured validation error that maps to the OpenAI-style "tool invocation" response. Adds streaming support so that when a tool emits partial output (logs, progress, incremental results), the compatibility layer wraps and streams these fragments as OpenAI-compatible assistant/tool messages (content-type: application/json+tool-output).

Compatibility notes: Backwards compatible for existing Redwood tool definitions. If a user presents OpenAI-style functions in the request, the mapper attempts a best-effort conversion; if conversion fails the runtime falls back to the original Redwood error path while returning a standardized compatibility error to the client. This PR preserves the existing API surface when not using openai-compat mode.

Implementation highlights: - redwood-openai-compat/src/tool-choice.ts: deterministic selection + tie-breaking rules; supports both explicit tool_choice strings and the older call-tool-by-name flow. - redwood-openai-compat/src/schema-mapper.ts: converts JSON Schema->Redwood param descriptors, maps oneOf/anyOf to union param types, flattens nested objects to allow both positional and named parameter styles when possible. - compat.ts: main adapter that produces OpenAI-compatible messages for: assistant.prompt->assistant/tool selection, tool invocation, tool output streaming, final tool response. - runtime/tooling changes: small hook in tool_executor.cpp to emit compatibility frames (non-breaking; gated behind openai-compat flag). - tests: unit and integration tests covering selection, schema edge cases, and streaming. - docs + SDK examples updated with recommended patterns and migration notes.

Checklist (what I did): - [x] Implemented deterministic tool_choice semantics consistent with OpenAI docs - [x] Schema mapping for required/optional fields, enums, and simple nested objects - [x] Streaming tool output formatting and tests for partial-output frames - [x] SDK example updates (Python/TS) and docs - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Added feature flag gating and config in helm chart

QA and testing notes: Ran full unit and integration suite. There was an intermittent failing test in streaming_tool_output.test.ts on CI (race in test harness) which was fixed by introducing a small 10ms backoff in the harness and added deterministic ordering assertions. E2E with example app confirmed that tool outputs are streamed as the OpenAI client expects (sequence of assistant messages with tool metadata), and that tool_choice resolution prefers explicit tool_choice when present, otherwise falls back to best-scored tool variant.

Known limitations and future work: - full support for complex JSON Schema features (deeply nested schemas, $ref resolution) will be addressed in a follow-up (ENG-4210) -perf: small added overhead when openai-compat mapping is enabled; we will add cache of mapped schemas in a subsequent PR - edge-case: when multiple tools expose identical signatures the tie-breaker is currently deterministic by lexicographic tool id; can be improved by adding model-provided scores in future.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on schema-mapper behavior and the streaming framing compatibility. The runtime change is intentionally minimal and gated; the majority of logic is in the compat adapter for easier audits.

Merge: squash and merge after approvals.
review_comments: Diego Chen: Can you add a test for tool_choice when multiple tools match with same score? Right now it looks like lexicographic tie-breaking which is fine but we should document it.
Ava Martinez (reply): Added tool_choice.tie_breaker test and documentation note in openai-compat docs. Kept lexicographic behavior for deterministic resolution.

Priya Natarajan: I see potential security concern: mapped schemas may accidentally expose internal-only params if names collide. Recommend we add a whitelist for exposed params OR require explicit opt-in on a per-tool basis.

Ava Martinez (reply): Good catch. Added explicit opt-in flag in openai-compat config (helm + runtime) and updated docs with recommended non-exposure practice. Also added unit tests to ensure opt-in gating is enforced.
Liam O'Connor: CI flaky test observed on first run (streaming_tool_output.test.ts). After rerun tests passed. Can you add a small note in changelog about the harness fix?
Ava Martinez (reply): Mentioned harness backoff fix in changelog and test comment.
release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: tool_choice semantics, tool schema mapping, and streaming tool output formatting. Backwards-compatible and gated by openai-compat feature flag. See openai-compat/tool-calling.md for migration instructions.
